svg.title: Anycast-RP: two RPs sharing one loopback address, and the MSDP message that makes the shared address work
svg.desc: A four-lane message sequence between the first-hop router, RP-1, RP-2 and the last-hop router, where both RPs carry the same RP address 10.0.0.1. Step one, the FHR sends a PIM Register with the source traffic unicast-encapsulated to RP-1. Step two, RP-1 forwards a source-active message to RP-2 over MSDP on TCP 639. Step three, the receiver's LHR sends a star-comma-group join, which the IGP resolves to the nearest RP, here RP-2. Step four, RP-2 sends a source-specific join toward the source, crossing RP-1 but remaining an ordinary PIM join. Step five, data follows the shortest path tree. A note explains that without MSDP, RP-2 knows the group but not the source, so the tree is built and no data ever arrives - a silent failure. A footer compares three implementations: MSDP-based anycast per RFC 4610, BGP-based anycast, and phantom RP, with the failover budget made of IGP convergence plus SA cache readiness.
svg.text: Anycast-RP: the address is shared, so the state has to be synchronised by hand
Both RPs own 10.0.0.1/32. IGP picks the nearest one per receiver - which is precisely why MSDP exists in this design.
FHR / source
LHR / receiver
1 Register (traffic unicast-encapsulated)
2 SA - source active, TCP 639
"source S is live for group G"
3 (*,G) Join - IGP walks it to RP-2
4 (S,G) Join toward the source
crosses RP-1, but it is only a PIM join - RP-1 is not consulted
5 data follows the SPT
Without step 2: RP-2 has the group from the join but has never heard of the source, so it builds a tree that leads nowhere. Every table looks right and no packet arrives.
THREE IMPLEMENTATIONS
MSDP-based (RFC 4610)
full mesh between the anycast RPs;
MSDP also carries the SA cache that
makes failover look instant
BGP-based anycast
source discovery rides in BGP;
no MSDP mesh to keep in step,
but vendor and profile support varies
Phantom RP
an RP address nobody owns, advertised
with a floating static route; simple,
5-30 s of failover, no SA cache

Failover budget = IGP/BFD detection + routing convergence + first Register from the new RP. Measure it with a real receiver, not with ping - and measure it for a NEW group, which has no cache to help it.
